original_value: The proliferation of massive open online courses (MOOCs) demands an effective way of personalized course recommendation. The recent attention-based recommendation models can distinguish the effects of different historical courses when recommending different target courses. However, when a user has interests in many different courses, the attention mechanism will perform poorly as the effects of the contributing courses are diluted by diverse historical courses. To address such a challenge, we propose a hierarchical reinforcement learning algorithm to revise the user profiles and tune the course recommendation model on the revised profiles.Systematically, we evaluate the proposed model on a real dataset consisting of 1,302 courses, 82,535 users and 458,454 user enrolled behaviors, which were collected from XuetangX—one of the largest MOOCs in China. Experimental results show that the proposed model significantly outperforms the state-of-the-art recommendation models (improving 5.02% to 18.95% in terms of HR@10).

result.paraphrase: The rapid growth of massive open online courses (MOOCs) creates a need for effective personalized course recommendation. Recent attention-based recommendation models can differentiate the influence of various historical courses when suggesting different target courses. However, for users interested in many different courses, the attention mechanism performs poorly because the contributions of those courses are diluted by a diverse course history. To address this issue, we propose a hierarchical reinforcement learning algorithm that revises user profiles and tunes the course recommendation model on the revised profiles. We systematically evaluate the proposed model on a real dataset containing 1,302 courses, 82,535 users, and 458,454 user enrollment behaviors collected from XuetangX, one of the largest MOOCs in China. Experimental results indicate that the proposed model significantly outperforms state-of-the-art recommendation models, improving HR@10 by 5.02% to 18.95%.
